Article Title: Govt distances itself from Hasina event but Dhaka not convinced
Article Text:
India has firmly denied any role in Sheikh Hasina's forthcoming media address, while Dhaka expresses skepticism, worried that the address may jeopardize diplomatic ties. Meanwhile, Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has received an invitation to the Brics summit from India, but he may encounter domestic backlash concerning the extradition of Hasina. To date, Bangladesh has not officially responded to the Brics invitation.

Ahead of former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina 's media address, the Indian government sought to distance itself from the event saying that India doesn't endorse the views that may be expressed at the event. However, Dhaka, which had raised the issue with Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi on Monday, remains unconvinced as diplomatic sources said allowing Hasina to make a political speech might rock an already unsteady relationship.Hasina, who has announced she plans to return to Bangladesh in December despite the death sentence awarded to her, is scheduled to virtually address a media event at the foreign correspondents' club on Wednesday evening. This would be Hasina's first media address since she fled to India after being deposed on August 5, 2024.The MEA said that the interaction was being organized by a private media entity. “The government has no involvement whatsoever in it. Neither does it endorse any views that may be expressed at the forum,” said spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal. The ministry recently told a Parliamentary committee that while providing refuge to Hasina, India had strictly adhered to the principle that no political activity is directed against any other country from Indian soil.The Indian government also for the first time confirmed that Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman had been invited by India for the BRICS summit that it will host in September. While PM Narendra Modi had earlier invited Rahman to India for a bilateral visit, the government said that the invitation on this occasion is for a BRICS outreach session and in Rahman's capacity as the current chair of BIMSTEC.While Bangladesh aspires for BRICS membership and has already received support from Russia and China for its candidature, Rahman will likely be wary of any domestic fallout of travelling to India amid the unresolved Hasina extradition issue. Jamaat-e-Islami's ascendancy as the primary opposition party may also restrict Rahman from soft-pedalling the Hasina issue. Dhaka has not yet formally accepted or declined the invitation that was extended by Modi to Rahman for BRICS.“You would be aware that a formal invitation for a bilateral visit to India was extended to the Bangladesh PM upon his assumption of office in Feb 2026. As far as the BRICS Summit is concerned, India has separately extended an invitation to Bangladesh PM in his capacity as the current Chair of BIMSTEC to attend the outreach session of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi,” said the spokesperson.“The invitation has been extended as per the standard practice being followed in BRICS for the outreach sessions. Other heads of regional groups have also been invited in a similar manner,” he added.
Article Summary: India has firmly denied any role in sheikh hasina's forthcoming media address. Dhaka expresses skepticism, worried that the address may jeopardize diplomatic ties. Bangladesh's prime minister tarique rahman has received an invitation to the brics summit from india.

Article Title: US Congressman warns FCRA Bill could affect India-US ties
Article Text:

A US lawmaker on Tuesday criticised the amendments proposed to India's foreign funding law, alleging that they could allow the government to take over churches and religious charities and warning that the issue could affect India-US ties.US Congressman Riley Moore said the proposed changes to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) amounted to "a clear attack against Christians" and urged India not to proceed with the legislation in its current form.In a post on X, the Republican Congressman from West Virginia said Christianity had a long history in India dating back to the arrival of St Thomas the Apostle on the Malabar Coast."But despite this long Christian history, India's Parliament is considering amending Foreign Contribution Regulation Amendment (FCRA) rules to permit government takeovers of churches and religious charities," Moore wrote."This is a clear attack against Christians. If this bill proceeds in this way, it would be a point of major concern in our bilateral relationship with India," he added.The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 proposes the creation of a Designated Authority that would take over the management of foreign contributions and assets created using such funds if an organisation's FCRA registration is cancelled, surrendered or lapses after not being renewed.The Bill specifies that where such assets include a place of worship, the Designated Authority must ensure that its religious character is preserved.It also proposes reducing the maximum punishment for violations of the Act from five years' imprisonment to one year.The FCRA regulates the receipt and utilisation of foreign contributions by NGOs, charitable trusts, educational institutions, religious bodies and other associations. According to the Ministry of Home Affairs, 13,520 organisations received foreign contributions worth Rs 55,741 crore between 2019 and 2022.Government data shows that as of July 15, 2026, there were 14,449 active FCRA registrations, while 22,498 had been cancelled and another 15,212 had expired.
Article Summary: Us congressman riley moore said the proposed changes to the foreign contribution (regulation) act (fcra) amounted to "a clear attack against christians" he urged india not to proceed with the legislation in its current form. According to the ministry of home affairs, 13,520 organisations received foreign contributions worth rs 55,741 crore between 2019 and 2022.

Article Title: Over 30 operatives killed by 'Indian agents' since 2020: LeT commander
Article Text:
Rizwan Hanif, a commander affiliated with Lashkar-e-Taiba, has alleged that Indian agents have systematically killed more than thirty individuals in different Pakistani locations since 2020. He characterized these murders as acts of religious persecution and rejected the authority of foreign entities. This statement comes amid heightened rhetoric from Pakistan's military, and experts suggest it serves as a strategic narrative amidst rising tensions.

In a significant public admission by terrorist organisation Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), senior commander Rizwan Hanif has claimed that over 30 members linked to the group have been killed across Pakistani cities since 2020 by "India agents". LeT members were targeted in Peshawar, Karachi, Rawalpindi, Muzaffarabad and Rawalakot, Hanif said while addressing a crowd in Pakistan.Attempting to frame these targeted killings as religious persecution, Hanif - the wanted deputy chief of Lashkar's POK unit - launched into inflammatory rhetoric. In a video circulated on social media, he questioned the group's "crime", asserting they were targeted solely for their faith.Hanif also launched a sharp attack against other faiths in his speech which was filmed by his followers and uploaded on social media.He declared that the outfit would continue its activities, rejecting the authority of foreign powers, including the US and Israel.The hate-filled speech comes on the heels of Lt General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, the official spokesperson of Pakistan armed forces (DG-ISPR), and the son of a US-designated terrorist peddling similar extremist views on a video while alleging that Afghans were not Muslims.Security experts saw these speeches as a face-saving narrative building exercise. The escalation in sectarian rhetoric comes as Islamabad faces mounting public unrest in Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir, where violent state crackdowns against anti-govt protesters at Rawalakot, in particular, and other places have drawn severe criticism while denting Pakistan's narrative about it being the champion of Kashmiris and their right to self-determination.Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif also labelled anti-govt demonstrators in POK as "enemies" comparable to India and ruled out any dialogue with them while defending the violent attacks on protesters.

Article Title: Indian cargo vessel sinks after attack in Yemeni waters; all 14 crew rescued
Article Text:
A projectile attack sank the Indian-flagged vessel off Yemen, but all 14 crew members, including 13 Indians, were safely rescued. (Representational image)

NEW DELHI: An Indian-flagged cargo vessel was struck by a projectile and sank off Yemen’s western coast on Tuesday. All 14 crew members aboard the vessel were rescued and brought to safety.Union minister for ports, shipping and waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, said the MSV Faize Noore Oliya was hit by a projectile in Yemeni waters, causing it to capsize and sink. The crew comprised 13 Indian nationals and one Yemeni sailor.The Yemeni Coast Guard rescued all 14 crew members and brought them safely to the port of Mokha, Sonowal added. No casualties were reported.Ministry of External Affairs said the vessel sank in the Red Sea off the Yemeni coast on August 4 and confirmed that all 13 Indian nationals had been rescued. The Indian Embassy in Riyadh was coordinating with Yemeni authorities to ensure the safety of the crew and provide necessary assistance.The government-affiliated National Resistance Forces said coast guard and naval units carried out a joint rescue operation after the vessel was attacked about 13 nautical miles (24 km) south of the Houthi-held port city of Hodeidah.The National Resistance Forces blamed Yemen’s Houthi rebels for the attack.The Houthis have not commented on the incident.Sonowal condemned what he called an “unprovoked attack” and said the safety of Indian seafarers remained the government’s “supreme priority”. He said the Director General of Maritime Administration had been instructed to coordinate with relevant agencies to ensure the security of Indian sailors in the region.The MEA also expressed concern over continued attacks on commercial shipping in the region, saying such targeting “must end”. It called for free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways in the region, in accordance with international law, to be restored at the earliest.
Article Summary: A projectile attack sank the indian-flagged vessel off yemen, but all 14 crew members, including 13 indians, were safely rescued. The crew comprised 13 indian nationals and one yemeni sailor. Ministry of external affairs said the vessel sank in the red sea off the yemeni coast on august 4.

Article Title: Sudden drop in altitude: Flyers injured as Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight encounters turbulence
Article Text:
Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi experienced turbulence-related event during cruise. (Photo: TOI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Some passengers and crew members onboard Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight (AI 2379) suffered injuries when the aircraft encountered turbulence Tuesday morning, causing a sudden drop in altitude by 300 feet. An AI with medical support received the 134 passengers onboard the Airbus A320 on arrival just after 11 am. Over 10 passengers and two crew members are learnt to have been taken to the Medanta medical centre at the airport. Subsequently, 14 injured - 10 passengers and four crew members - were shifted to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram and India Spinal Injury Centre in Vasant Kunj.An AI spokesperson said the aircraft “experienced a brief in-flight turbulence-related event during cruise, resulting in a momentary change in altitude. The aircraft landed safely in Delhi and all passengers and crew have safely disembarked. There have been no serious injuries reported as of now. A small number of passengers and crew members with minor injuries requiring medical assessment have been taken to a medical facility at the airport for precautionary examination and care by Air India’s airport team and medical personnel.The A320 had taken off from Phuket at 8.27 am and landed in Delhi just after 11 am (all timings local).“The safety and well-being of our passengers and crew remain Air India’s highest priority. We are providing all necessary support to those affected and are cooperating fully with the relevant authorities as part of the investigation,” the spokesperson added.Aircraft frequently experience clear air turbulence (CAT), which International Civil Aviation Organisation defines as turbulence generated in clear air, in regions without clouds that is invisible to the pilot and by the US Federal Aviation Administration as sudden severe turbulence occurring in cloudless regions that causes violent buffeting of aircraft. Due to this possibility, it is advisable to have seatbelt loosely on during flight.
Article Summary: Air india flight from phuket to delhi experienced turbulence-related event during cruise. The aircraft landed safely in delhi and all passengers and crew have safely disembarked. Over 10 passengers and two crew members are learnt to have been taken to the medanta medical centre at the airport.

Article Title: 'Will do whatever is necessary for national interest': India after Pakistan deploys 250 Chinese Howitzers
Article Text:
File photo: Chinese self-propelled artillery guns

Pakistan deploys Chinese SH-15 howitzers

India also modernising artillery

NEW DELHI: India on Tuesday said it would do "whatever is necessary" to safeguard its national interests after reports emerged that Pakistan had deployed a large number of Chinese-made SH-15 self-propelled artillery guns along the border facing India.Responding to a question during the ministry of external affairs' weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India's position remained unchanged on cross-border terrorism and asserted that the country would remain prepared to defend itself."During Operation Sindoor, we saw how a befitting reply was given (to Pakistan). From our side, our stance is that cross-border terrorism must stop, and we will do whatever is necessary in our national interest, for which we always remain vigilantly deployed," Jaiswal said.The remarks came a day after reports said Pakistan had deployed around 250 Chinese-origin SH-15 wheeled self-propelled howitzers in formations facing India as part of its artillery modernisation programme.In the briefing, Jaiswal also strongly criticised the recently held elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK), describing them as a "complete farce" and accusing Pakistan of using force to suppress public dissent."This so-called local election in PoK is a complete farce. The real happening is that of public protests and wanton killings by Pakistani forces. Such hollow exercises cannot hide reality," Jaiswal said.He said that at least 90 civilians had been killed since June during the crackdown in PoK."Since June this year, at least 90 civilians have lost their lives in the continuing crackdown. The Pakistani Establishment has answered public discontent with bullets, blackouts, intimidation and repression, and now seeks to manufacture legitimacy through a hollow electoral exercise," he said, urging the international community to hold Islamabad accountable.Jaiswal also responded to a media inquiry about a viral video in which members of the Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba claimed that 30 to 40 of their commanders had been killed, alleging that Indian agencies were responsible for the killings.He said, "We continue to call upon all countries to take strong action against cross-border terrorism and those who promote it. We also call upon Pakistan to take decisive action against cross-border terrorism and dismantle the terrorist infrastructure operating from its soil."Pakistan ordered 236 SH-15 155mm/52-calibre wheeled self-propelled artillery guns from Chinese state-owned defence firm Norinco in 2019, with deliveries beginning in 2022 and a second batch arriving in 2023.Pakistan has also acquired a transfer of technology agreement to manufacture the artillery system at Heavy Industries Taxila.The SH-15, known as the PCL-181 in China, has reportedly been deployed mainly in Pakistan's Gujranwala, Sialkot and Jalalpur Jattan sectors opposite India, particularly around the Shakargarh Bulge.The guns were also used during Operation Sindoor.The 155mm artillery system is capable of firing multiple types of ammunition and has a range of more than 50 kilometres when using rocket-assisted projectiles.Retired Lieutenant General PR Shankar, former Director General of Artillery, told TOI that the acquisition strengthens Pakistan's conventional firepower and complements its Army Rocket Force, enhancing its long-range strike capabilities.The deployment comes as India continues to modernise its own artillery under the Field Artillery Rationalisation Plan.The Indian Army has inducted 155mm artillery systems such as the M777 ultra-light howitzer, the K-9 Vajra self-propelled gun and the indigenous Dhanush gun. It has also placed orders for 307 Advanced Towed Artillery Gun Systems (ATAGS), developed domestically.India is also working on a wheeled Mounted Gun System (MGS), based on the ATAGS platform, which is currently in the advanced stages of development and has undergone initial firing trials.
Article Summary: Pakistan deploys chinese-made sh-15 self-propelled artillery guns along the border facing india. India's position remained unchanged on cross-border terrorism and asserted that the country would remain prepared to defend itself. India also strongly criticised the recently held elections in pakistan-occupied jammu and kashmir (pok) as a "complete farce"

Article Title: Government to grill Meta brass on child abuse, AI content
Article Text:
In an important meeting scheduled for this week, government officials will confront Meta executives regarding pressing issues. The discussions will center around the presence of child sexual abuse material, the rise of AI-created content, and the measures in place for takedowns involving notable personalities. Compliance with local laws and the efficiency of Meta's content moderation efforts, particularly in monitoring synthetic content, are also poised to be key topics of concern.

Want to know how Meta is tackling CSAM: Govt

NEW DELHI: Govt will press Meta on child sexual abuse material, AI-generated content and safeguards around takedown of posts by prominent personalities, including PM Modi, when the company's senior executives meet officials here this week, reports Aabhas Sharma.MeitY secretary S Krishnan said Meta executives, including Joel Kaplan, head of Meta's public policy, are expected to meet govt officials on Wednesday and Thursday, with discussions set to cover compliance with Indian laws, content moderation and challenges posed by AI content.MeitY secretary S Krishnan said Tuesday, “We want to ensure that compliance happens. There are a range of issues.”He said govt wants to know what measures Meta has taken to tackle CSAM on its platforms and how effectively it is monitoring synthetically generated content. “CSAM issue has been raised, and we want to know what measures have been taken to address it. We also want to understand to what extent synthetically-generated content is being monitored,” he said.Krishnan also flagged concerns over the removal of content posted by verified accounts of prominent personalities, saying that such actions should be backed by stronger safeguards.
Article Summary: Meity secretary s krishnan said meta executives are expected to meet govt officials on wednesday and thursday. He said govt wants to know what measures meta has taken to tackle csam on its platforms. Krishnan also flagged concerns over the removal of content posted by verified accounts of prominent personalities.

Article Title: Big clean energy milestone: NPCIL cumulatively generates over 1,000 bn units of N-power, avoids 860 million tons of CO2 emissions
Article Text:
India has achieved a remarkable milestone in clean energy, generating over one thousand billion units from nuclear power. This achievement helps avoid more than 860 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions. The government aims to increase nuclear power capacity to 100 GW by 2047, with an intermediate target of 22 GW by 2031-32. This expansion will involve multiple stakeholders and the introduction of new legislation.

NEW DELHI: In a milestone for India’s clean energy production, Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) has cumulatively generated over 1,000 billion units of nuclear electricity.NPCIL said Tuesday, “Since commencement of commercial operation, NPCIL’s nuclear power plants have cumulatively generated over 1,000 billion units of clean electricity, thereby avoiding over 860 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions into the environment.”“This milestone reflects NPCIL’s steadfast commitment to deliver safe, reliable and sustainable nuclear power, strengthening India’s energy security while supporting the nation’s clean energy transition and climate goals,” it said on XTo give the scale of how much carbon emission is avoided, a typical passenger vehicle emits about 4.6 metric tonnes of CO2 per year. Avoiding 860 million tonnes is equal to taking roughly 187 million gasoline-powered cars going off the road for an entire year. At least 860 million tonnes is roughly equivalent to the total annual greenhouse gas emissions of a major industrial country like Germany or Japan for a full year.Govt has drawn up a roadmap for reaching the 100 GW nuclear power capacity in the next two decades by 2047, as announced in the Nuclear Energy Mission in the Budget 2025-26, thereby increasing the share of reliable, low-carbon base-load nuclear energy in the country’s energy mix and reaching the goal of net zero carbon emissions by 2070.The present nuclear power capacity of 8.78 GW is expected to reach about 22 GW by 2031-32 on progressive completion of projects presently at various stages of implementation. Another 32 GW of nuclear power capacity is envisaged to be set up beyond 2032 by NPCIL under the administrative control of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE).This will comprise indigenous pressurised heavy water reactors (PHWRs) and light water reactors (LWRs) planned to be set up by 2047, taking NPCIL’s nuclear power capacity to 54 GW.The balance of 46 GW comprising reactors of different technologies, is expected to be set up by other public sector enterprises, private sector and joint ventures in different business models. With the govt enacting the SHANTI Act (Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India Act, 2025) last year, the new law provides the legal framework that makes this 46 GW expansion possible.
Article Summary: India has achieved a remarkable milestone in clean energy, generating over one thousand billion units from nuclear power. This achievement helps avoid more than 860 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions. The government aims to increase nuclear power capacity to 100 gw by 2047.

Article Title: Terror suspects spotted, search ops launched in J&K’s Poonch
Article Text:
Following intelligence indicating potential terror suspects in Poonch, security forces have launched coordinated operations in two strategic locations. Reports have confirmed sightings near Gujjar Naar and Kherowali dhok, prompting a thorough search in the isolated Dhara Sangla village by army and police units. As of Tuesday evening, no contact with the suspects has been reported. Earlier, a significant search initiative was executed in the Thanamandi area of Rajouri district.

JAMMU: Security forces on Tuesday initiated joint cordon-and-search operations in two locations in J&K’s Poonch district after being alerted about the alleged movement of terror suspects.According to intelligence inputs, three terror suspects were seen near Gujjar Naar area, and four more were spotted close to Kherowali dhok (high-altitude temporary huts constructed by nomads) in the remote Dhara Sangla village in Surankote sector.Troops of the Army’s 16 Rashtriya Rifles and J&K Police’s Special Operations Group subsequently launched intensive searches. No contact was established with the terror suspects till Tuesday evening, even as both operations remained underway, officials said.Earlier on July 14, a massive combing operation was carried out across multiple villages in Rajouri district’s Thanamandi after CCTV footage purportedly captured the movement of two terror suspects in the area.

Article Title: After opening golf tournament, CM Omar says authorities must not allow repeat of migrant worker killings
Article Text:
Omar Abdullah, the chief minister of Jammu and Kashmir, strongly condemned the recent violence against migrant laborers, emphasizing that such acts are unacceptable and calling for heightened security measures. He also underscored the significance of golf tournaments as a means to boost tourism in the area, recalling a time when these events were a hallmark of Kashmir's serene landscape, well before militancy took root.

SRINAGAR: Jammu & Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah said on Tuesday that the recent attack on migrant labourers in south Kashmir’s Kulgam district “should not have happened” and that those responsible for maintaining security must ensure such incidents do not recur.“It is a matter of great regret… Innocent people were killed, and no religion permits such acts. No amount of condemnation or words is enough to denounce this attack,” Omar said.Under the Union Territory arrangement, law and order and security is looked after by lieutenant-governor Manoj Sinha.On July 31, terrorists had shot and killed two migrant labourers in Kulgam district. On July 23, a terrorist had shot J&K head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi dead in south Kashmir’s Anantnag, the first attack in Kashmir since the Pahalgam massacre that left 26 people dead on April 22 last year.The chief minister, speaking after inaugurating the fifth edition of the J&K Open 2026 DP World Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI), said the golf tournament is an important part of his govt’s broader strategy to promote tourism. “Even without actively promoting golf tourism, we have started seeing what we want, people flying into Srinagar for a long weekend of golf,” he said.When asked about Article 370 and whether its abrogation has brought any change, like holding such tournaments, Omar initially declined to comment, saying the issue was unrelated to the event. He, however, said golf tournaments were organised regularly in Kashmir long before Article 370 was abrogated, and even before militancy began. “Golf tournaments were being organised in Kashmir even in the 1980s, much before militancy,” he said.

Article Title: CPI (ML) L whose students wing was at forefront of Gen Z protests wants voting age lowered to 16
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Liberation, whose student wing All India Students Association (AISA) was at the forefront in the Cockroach Janta Party led protests at Jantar Mantar, has demanded that the voting age should be lowered to 16 from 18 years to empower the younger lot among Gen Z.This comes in the backdrop of the students protests that succeeded in getting Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign. For the Left parties like CPI(ML)L, the victory of their student outfits in raising the issues affecting Gen Z, has emboldened them and provided an opportunity to connect with the students to take up their concerns related to education, employment and accountability.Attacking the govt over its use of force against protesters, CPI(ML) L general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya said, “In the protests at Jantar Mantar the world saw an awakening where Gen Z came out to talk about the things that affect them and sought accountability. I feel they are ready and therefore I feel voting age must be lowered,” Bhattacharya said.The voting age in India was brought down from 21 to 18 years through ‘The Constitution (Sixty-first Amendment) Act, 1988. While in most countries the age of voting is 18, in some countries like Argentina, Austria, Brazil, Cuba, Ecuador, Nicaragua, East Timor, Greece, and Indonesia 16 or 17 year olds can vote.Bhattacharya in a statement released by the party on Tuesday said that if the RSS really wants to listen to India’s Gen Z, they should lower the voting age to 16.In today's digital era of information revolution, 16-year-olds are informed enough to make their political choices,” he said.“RSS is reportedly quite desperate to reach out to Gen Z. Mohan Bhagwat is all set to address 2,000 students aged 15 to 19 brought from 100 cities on August 6 at Mumbai’s Nita Mukesh Ambani Centre! The numbers are impressive, but what will be the outreach about?,” Bhattacharya asked.“Modi (PM Narendra Modi) has already talked about ‘culture shock’, invoking patriarchal prejudices against India’s ‘misled daughters’. The orchestrated backlash, both online and offline, is forcing 15-year-olds to offer apology videos,” he alleged.With this attack on the ruling dispensation, CPI(ML)L has set the pitch for its outreach to Gen Z. “In the protests at Jantar Mantar the world saw an awakening where Gen Z came out to talk about the things that affect them and sought accountability. I feel they are ready and therefore I feel voting age must be lowered,” Bhattacharya said.He said that since he raised the demand on Tuesday, he has received positive responses from the youth. Bhattacharya plans to not only discuss this with AISA members but also take it up with Left parties - CPI(M) and CPI(ML) and also INDIA bloc members.Meanwhile, all set to keep up the momentum generated by the protests, the Left parties CPM, CPI(ML)L and CPI are working on stepping up coordination for the outreach among various sections at the grassroots including students. "The Left needs to coordinate with more focus as a group on issues and align with movements led by students, workers, women and farmers across states. To enable this we are working on a plan and a series of meetings have been held to discuss how we can improve coordination," Bhattacharya said.
Article Summary: The communist party of india (marxist-leninist) liberation has demanded that the voting age should be lowered to 16 from 18 years. This comes in the backdrop of the students protests that succeeded in getting union minister dharmendra pradhan to resign.

Article Title: SC calls to 'dismantle' ‘men’s clubs’ in Bar Councils, orders co-option of 2 women members
Article Text:
SC directs high court CJs to nominate co-opted women members

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday observed that State Bar Councils have increasingly become “men’s clubs” and said the monopoly over their representation and functioning must be dismantled.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the remarks while hearing petitions related to elections to the Bar Council of India and State Bar Councils.“Bar Councils have become men’s clubs. We may observe that people take it like a monopoly. This has to be completely dismantled,” CJI Surya Kant remarked during the hearing.The court directed the Chief Justices of the jurisdictional High Courts to nominate two women members to every State Bar Council through co-option. One must be a former woman High Court judge and the other a senior woman advocate with a fair standing at the Bar.The court said the nominated members should have no connection with the election process so that they can function independently and impartially.“As far as co-option is concerned...10% we always had in mind. There should be co-option of those who don't have anything to do with elections,” the court observed.The Supreme Court also clarified that a woman who unsuccessfully contested a State Bar Council election would not be barred from being considered for co-option.The court referred the issue of the methodology for calculating transferable votes, particularly for women candidates, to the High-Powered Supervisory Committee headed by former Supreme Court judge Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia. The committee will reconsider the methodology after inviting suggestions from members of the Bar and giving them an opportunity for an oral hearing.The Supreme Court had earlier directed that women should have 30 per cent% representation in State Bar Councils, with 20 per cent of the seats filled through direct elections and the remaining 10 per cent through co-option where required.The High-Powered Supervisory Committee was constituted by the court to oversee elections to the Bar Council of India and State Bar Councils and deal with election-related disputes.
Article Summary: Sc directs high court cjs to nominate co-opted women members to every state bar council. One must be a former woman high court judge and the other a senior woman advocate with a fair standing at the bar. The court said the nominated members should have no connection with the election process so that they can function independently.

Massive anti-terror search underway in Poonch

Unexploded mortar shell recovered near border

Comes amid heightened tensions along India-Pakistan border

NEW DELHI: Security forces on Tuesday launched a search operation after a Pakistani drone was spotted hovering over forward villages along the International Border in Jammu and Kashmir's Kathua district.The development comes amid heightened security concerns along the border following reports of Pakistan strengthening its military deployment opposite India.The drone intruded into Indian territory around 2 pm and was seen hovering over the forward villages of Shukhmal, Devindera and Tapan in the Bobiyan area of Kathua's Hiranagar sector.Alert Border Security Force (BSF) personnel immediately initiated countermeasures to bring down the drone.However, the flying object, which was at a high altitude, managed to return across the border before it could be intercepted.Following the incident, the BSF and Jammu and Kashmir Police launched an extensive search operation to ensure that the drone had not dropped any weapons, explosives or other material.The operation was continuing at the time of the last reports, according to news agency PTI.Separately, security forces also launched a large-scale cordon-and-search operation across dozens of remote villages in Poonch district following intelligence inputs about the suspected movement of two groups of terrorists.Personnel from the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the Jammu and Kashmir Police, assisted by the Rashtriya Rifles, carried out searches in villages including Dhara Sangla, Gujjar Naar and Kherowali Dhok in Surankote tehsil.Officials said no contact had yet been established with the suspected terrorists, while systematic searches were continuing in the densely forested region.Security personnel also searched Kalaban and adjoining areas in Mendhar tehsil, but no arrests were made.In another security-related development, an old rusted mortar shell was recovered from the courtyard of a house in Kattal-Brahmana village in Kathua's Hiranagar sector on Tuesday morning.Labourers carrying out excavation work at the residence noticed the suspicious object and informed the authorities. A police team, along with the Bomb Disposal Squad (BDS), secured the area and safely removed the unexploded shell for disposal.The recent drone intrusion occurs during a time of heightened tension along the border. Earlier today, India said it would do "whatever is necessary" to safeguard its national interests following reports that Pakistan had deployed around 250 Chinese-origin SH-15 self-propelled artillery guns along sectors facing India.Responding to the reports during the ministry of external affairs' weekly briefing on Tuesday, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, "During Operation Sindoor, we saw how a befitting reply was given (to Pakistan). From our side, our stance is that cross-border terrorism must stop, and we will do whatever is necessary in our national interest, for which we always remain vigilantly deployed."The Chinese-made SH-15 155mm/52-calibre artillery systems have been deployed primarily in Pakistan's Gujranwala, Sialkot and Jalalpur Jattan sectors opposite India as part of Islamabad's artillery modernisation programme.The latest incident follows another suspected Pakistani drone sighting reported in Rajouri district last month. Blinking lights were seen over forward villages in the Sunderbani sector before the suspected unmanned aerial vehicle returned towards Pakistan.Security forces had subsequently conducted a search operation to check for any airdropped payload but found nothing suspicious.Earlier in June, Army personnel had also opened fire after spotting a Pakistani drone over forward posts in the Balakote sector of Poonch, forcing it to retreat towards Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.
Article Summary: Pakistani drone spotted hovering over forward villages along the international border in jammu and kashmir's kathua district. Security forces launch extensive search operation to ensure that the drone had not dropped any weapons, explosives or other material.

Article Title: 'Private media entity organising it': Govt says 'no role' in Sheikh Hasina's proposed August 5 event
Article Text:
Former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina has been living in Delhi since August 5, 2025 (File photo/AP)

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Tuesday said the government has no involvement in a proposed media event to be attended by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina , stressing that it is being organised by a "private media entity" and that New Delhi does not endorse any views that may be expressed at the forum.The event is scheduled for Wednesday, on the second anniversary of Sheikh Hasina's resignation as Bangladesh prime minister. She stepped down on August 5, 2024, following weeks of student-led protests and has been living in Delhi since then."The interaction you refer to is being organised by a private media entity. The government has no involvement whatsoever in it. Neither does it endorse any views that may be expressed at the forum," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told reporters during a bi-weekly media briefing.His remarks came a day after Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs, Shama Obaed Islam, asked New Delhi to clarify its stand on a possible public appearance by the Awami League chief.“We are moving forward with India with a forward-looking approach. We don’t want it to be damaged, and I firmly believe that India doesn’t want it either. So, India has to clarify whether it is supporting it or not,” she said while addressing reporters at the ministry of foreign affairs in Dhaka.The issue was also discussed during a meeting between Bangladesh's foreign affairs adviser Humayun Kabir and India's newly appointed High Commissioner to Dhaka, Dinesh Trivedi, on Monday.The event at the Foreign Correspondents' Club of South Asia in New Delhi will mark Sheikh Hasina's first public appearance since her ouster. The former prime minister, who recently announced plans to return to Bangladesh by December, has been sentenced to death by an International Crimes Tribunal in Dhaka for "crimes against humanity" in connection with her government's crackdown on student protesters.She has rejected the verdict, calling it political vendetta.
Article Summary: The event is scheduled for wednesday, on the second anniversary of sheikh hasina's resignation as bangladesh prime minister. She stepped down on august 5, 2024, following weeks of student-led protests and has been living in delhi since then.

Article Title: 'Answered public discontent with bullets and repression': MEA slams Pakistan over 'farce' PoK polls
Article Text:
MEA spokersperson called the PoK polls 'farce' and slammed Pakistan to pay heed to the atrocities committed by the Pak establishment

NEW DELHI: The Ministry of External Affairs on Tuesday slammed the recently conducted so-called local elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK), calling them “a complete farce” and accusing Pakistani forces of using violence, blackouts, intimidation and repression against civilians.Addressing a media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, “The real happening is that of public protests and wanton killings by Pakistani forces. Such hollow exercises cannot hide reality.”Jaiswal claimed that at least 90 civilians had been killed since June during what he described as a continuing crackdown by the Pakistani establishment.“Since June this year, at least 90 civilians have lost their lives in the continuing crackdown,” he said. “The Pakistani Establishment has answered public discontent with bullets, blackouts, intimidation and repression, and now seeks to manufacture legitimacy through a hollow electoral exercise.”He urged the international community to hold Islamabad accountable, saying, “the world should see through the flimsy veneer of Pakistan's hypocritical lecturing on human rights.”The comments followed protests and disruptions surrounding the PoK elections, with demonstrations reported across the region.Human rights and press freedom groups have also raised concerns over alleged state violence, restrictions on the media and internet shutdowns during the protests.Separately, the MEA called on Pakistan to take “decisive action” against cross-border terrorism while responding to a viral video showing Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba members claiming that 30-40 of their commanders had been killed and alleging that Indian agencies were behind the killings.“We continue to call upon all countries to take strong action against cross-border terrorism and those who promote it,” Jaiswal said.“We also call upon Pakistan to take decisive action against cross-border terrorism and dismantle the terrorist infrastructure operating from its soil,” he added.The remarks came amid heightened scrutiny of Pakistan's handling of terrorism and its actions in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir.
Article Summary: Mea spokersperson called the pok polls 'farce' and slammed pakistan to pay heed to the atrocities committed by the pak establishment. At least 90 civilians had been killed since june during what he described as a continuing crackdown by the pakistani establishment.

Article Title: Russian drone chases Ukrainian vegetable seller in 'safari' attack - Watch
Article Text:
Russian drone targets Ukrainian vegetable seller in 'Safari' attack

Ukraine on Tuesday accused Russia of committing a war crime after footage emerged showing a Russian drone pursuing and striking a vegetable seller in the southern city of Kherson, leaving the civilian wounded.Video footage shows a drone pursuing a man around a van being used as a roadside vegetable stall before exploding as he dives behind the vehicle for cover. Police said the man, in his 50s, survived the attack but sustained shrapnel injuries and suffered shock.Reacting to the incident, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the latest footage highlighted what he described as Russia's continued targeting of civilians in Kherson."Today, many were shocked by yet another video of the drone 'safari' Russians are carrying out against civilians in Kherson," Zelenskyy said in a post on X, adding that "Russia has gone mad" and calling for increased pressure on Moscow and strong security guarantees for Ukraine."The world must see this. It must see every piece of evidence that Russia has gone mad and that its soldiers take pleasure in killing and abusing civilians.Without pressure on Russia, the dismantling of its capacity for aggression, and real security guarantees, it is simply impossible to imagine the world being able to coexist with this evil. We must remain resolute in defending life. We must act and support life in ways that force Russia to seriously think about peace rather than expanding the range of its drones," Zelenskyy added.Ukrainian authorities later identified the victim only as 52-year-old Yurii and released a video interview with him from the hospital.According to Oleksandr Prokudin head of the Kherson regional military administration, Yurii had travelled to Kherson that morning to sell vegetables. Prokudin shared the hospital interview on Telegram.Yurii said he and his wife were arranging crates of vegetables beside their van when he heard the distinctive buzz of a drone overhead. As his wife fled, he said, the drone turned its attention to him. He recalled holding up several heads of garlic toward the drone's camera to signal to its operator that he was not filming it."It could see that I had tomatoes out, some cucumbers and eggplants laid out on the floor," Yurii said, as cited by the BBC. "It even ducked under the umbrella when I was running away round the other side."So-called "safari" attacks, in which drones are allegedly used to hunt civilians, have been reported in Kherson for months. The southern city lies just a few miles from the front line.A 2025 United Nations report said it found that Russian armed forces had "recurrently killed and injured civilians" in the area by using drones to target them.Ukraine has also carried out drone and long-range missile strikes inside Russia, which Russian authorities say have resulted in civilian casualties.Russia on Monday accused Ukraine of carrying out a "terrorist" attack after seven people, including three children, were killed at the Black Sea resort town of Gelendzhik in what Moscow described as a deliberate drone strike targeting civilians.
Article Summary: Russian drone targets ukrainian vegetable seller in 'safari' attack. Video footage shows a drone pursuing a man around a van being used as a roadside vegetable stall. The man, in his 50s, survived the attack but sustained shrapnel injuries and suffered shock. "so-called "safari" attacks have been reported in kherson for months.

Article Title: Man arrested with gun, ammunition near Trump's California golf course ahead of fundraiser
Article Text:
Armed man held near Trump golf course after allegedly monitoring security preparations

A 38-year-old man was arrested near President Donald Trump's Los Angeles-area golf course after authorities alleged he was monitoring security preparations ahead of Trump's fundraising event at the venue, the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department said.The man, identified as Jeanine John Taele, was detained on Sunday after deputies found a 16-round magazine with ammunition in his pocket. Authorities also recovered a loaded pistol from his vehicle. Investigators later searched his home in the nearby city of Downey and seized multiple firearms, magazines, ammunition, body armour and notebooks containing what officials described as "concerning statements."The arrest was announced as Trump prepared to attend a fundraising dinner for the Republican National Committee at Trump National Golf Course in Rancho Palos Verdes, south of Los Angeles.According to the sheriff's department, Taele had been taking photographs and recording videos around the golf course while appearing to monitor security arrangements two days before the event.Taele has been charged with several felony offences, including second-degree robbery, receiving a large-capacity magazine and possession of a short-barrelled rifle or shotgun.He also faces a misdemeanor charge of carrying a concealed firearm in a vehicle.He pleaded not guilty to all charges on Monday. A court ordered him to stay away from the golf course and prohibited him from possessing weapons. His bail was set at $250,000.Authorities said Taele was already under investigation by the El Segundo Police Department in connection with a robbery case when deputies contacted him on Sunday.The sheriff's department said there is "no credible threat to our communities."The arrest comes more than a year after a jury in 2025 found a man guilty of attempting to assassinate Trump at the president's Florida golf club.
Article Summary: Armed man held near trump golf course after allegedly monitoring security preparations. The man, identified as jeanine john taele, was detained on sunday. Deputies found a 16-round magazine with ammunition in his pocket. Authorities also recovered a loaded pistol from his vehicle.

Article Title: Indian refiners maximise: Fuel exports hit 1-yr high as robust margins, Russia diesel export ban help
Article Text:
The July export shipment volume was the highest recorded for the month since Kpler began tracking the data in 2017.

Middle East conflict and evolving trade patterns

Amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict, India’s fuel exports have hit a 1-year high. Exports of refined petroleum products climbed to a one-year high in July, supported by strong diesel refining margins, Russia's ban on diesel exports and abundant crude availability during the temporary ceasefire in the Iran conflict. This enabled domestic refiners to increase overseas shipments.According to shipping data from analytics firm Kpler, India exported 1.53 million barrels per day (bpd) of refined fuels during July. This is about 27% higher than the average monthly volume over the previous 12 months. Incidentally, India’s crude oil imports from Russia also hit an all-time high of 2.8 million barrels per day in July.The July export shipment volume was the highest recorded for the month since Kpler began tracking the data in 2017."Exceptionally strong diesel margins, following the ban on Russian diesel exports, incentivised exports (from India), with cargoes headed to regions previously supplied by West Asia and Russia to fill the supply void," Nikhil Dubey, lead analyst for refining at Kpler told ET.The conflicts in West Asia and Europe have significantly altered global fuel trade patterns by lifting prices and opening new export opportunities.Supply disruptions affecting Russia and Gulf producers, two of the world's major suppliers of refined petroleum products, have reshaped international trade flows.Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries have compelled Moscow to halt exports of petrol and diesel, increasing its reliance on imports, including supplies from India, to meet domestic fuel requirements. According to Dubey, countries such as Turkey, which have traditionally depended on Russian fuel, are now replacing those supplies with cargoes from India."Europe remains short on diesel supplies and typically relies on imports from West Asia; however, those supplies are currently constrained due to regional turmoil," he noted, adding that record-high diesel refining margins had encouraged higher export volumes to Europe.Exports also received a boost from "ample crude availability following the arrival of stranded cargoes that were released during the brief Iran-US truce," Dubey said, noting that the additional crude supported higher refinery utilisation rates.He added that the completion of maintenance shutdowns at refineries operated by Reliance Industries (RIL) and Nayara Energy enabled both companies to process larger volumes of crude.Reliance Industries accounts for nearly three-fourths of India's refined fuel exports. Nayara Energy, backed by Rosneft and the country's other major fuel exporter, reportedly exported petroleum products to Russia last month.
Article Summary: India exported 1.53 million barrels per day (bpd) of refined fuels during july. This is about 27% higher than the average monthly volume over the previous 12 months. The july export shipment volume was the highest recorded for the month since kpler began tracking the data in 2017.

Article Title: What is 'Operation Fortress'? Reform UK's military plan to stop migrants crossing English Channel
Article Text:
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage unveiled 'Operation Fortress'.

What is Operation Fortress?

Ceuta crisis cited as warning for Europe

Experts question feasibility

Why is Reform UK pushing the plan now?

Britain and France already have migration pact

Britain's right-wing Reform UK party has unveiled 'Operation Fortress', a military-led plan that it says would end illegal migrant crossings across the English Channel if it comes to power.Party leader Nigel Farage described it as the "largest military operation in the Channel since World War II," promising to deploy the Royal Navy to intercept small boats and return migrants to France.Under the proposed policy, the Royal Navy would be tasked with intercepting migrant boats attempting to cross the English Channel and escorting them back to France. Reform UK claims the operation would make Britain's borders "impenetrable" and end small-boat crossings within weeks."Under a Reform government, within a fortnight, there would be no more boats," Farage said while unveiling the plan.Announcing the proposal on Monday, Farage pointed to the recent migrant surge in Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, saying the crisis highlighted the rising challenge of irregular migration across Europe.Last week, thousands of migrants attempted to enter Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco, putting fresh pressure on Spanish authorities and reigniting the debate over Europe's border security.Reform UK argued that Britain must act before facing a similar situation, using the developments in Ceuta as justification for its tougher border strategy.The proposal, however, drew immediate criticism from military experts and political opponents, who questioned both its legality and practicality.Andrew Fox, a former British paratrooper and senior associate fellow at the Henry Jackson Society think tank, said the plan overlooked key legal and operational hurdles, news agency Reuters reported.According to Fox, British warships cannot enter French territorial waters, seize migrant boats or disembark passengers in France without Paris' consent.Former Royal Navy commander Tom Sharpe also dismissed the proposal, saying naval vessels are not designed to function as "passenger ferries" and cannot simply return migrants against France's wishes.The announcement comes as Reform UK faces scrutiny over donations and financial disclosures involving senior party figures, with recent opinion polls showing the party losing its lead after more than a year.Labour accused Reform of recycling old immigration proposals to divert attention from questions over its finances.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has also vowed "relentless" action to curb small-boat crossings after more than 2,000 migrants reportedly arrived in Britain during the first two weeks of his premiership.Britain and France signed a three-year agreement earlier this year under which London will provide up to 766 million euros to help France strengthen efforts to prevent small-boat crossings across the Channel.Despite those measures, migration remains one of Britain's most controversial political issues, with thousands continuing to attempt the dangerous sea crossing each year.
Article Summary: Reform uk leader nigel farage unveils 'operation fortress' plan. Royal navy to intercept small boats and return migrants to france. Reform uk claims the operation would make britain's borders "impenetrable" critics say the plan overlooks key legal and operational hurdles.
